name: build-add
what: Ownership added: the day runs again with it, its card is on the canvas beside the flows shipped, and its sheet says it was added here, what it reads and what it gives

#sheet: Added here from the catalogue: built from the day’s run, and part of the flow as kept in this browser.

name: build-explore
what: What the added flow gives, explored as any dataset is: the applications by business unit, a card a column

name: build-inside
what: The added flow entered, as any flow read is: its own notebook as a box, and the flows it reads as cards

name: build-join-form
what: The join form, from what a flow gives: apps, explored from Applications' sheet, its How it joins, and Join it with another dataset. The form has the two datasets, the key on each side, the rows kept and the columns to take, and says it writes a cell of the flow's own; the key is the one the ontology's link gives: the owning team's id names an organisational unit
clicks: Each application with its owning unit

name: build-join-refused
what: The form refuses what the run would stop on, before anything is written: apps joined with the TLS feed, which a held day can fill from another day, with filled_from left out. Everything built from such a feed says which rows came from another day (ADR 0009 amendment 1)

.vf-detail .jf-err: tls_checked is built from a feed a held day can fill from another day: take filled_from, so the rows that came from another day say so.
.vf-detail: Columns from tls_checked

name: build-join-written
what: The join written: the form opened again, the other dataset picked, the key the ontology's link gives left as it is, the cell written in joins.nb.ts and read back by the notebook parser, the day run again, and the joined dataset open on its Explore tab; its notebook is a box on the canvas, as every notebook is
clicks: Each application with its owning unit

name: build-record
what: The record says both: the flow added from the catalogue, and the join in words
